title: The Chipping pub steeped in village history and 'haunted' by ghosts from the 1800s

content:
A Chipping pub steeped in village history is said to have a ghostly past — with the story of a woman who died there more than a century ago still hanging over the building.

The Sun Inn, in Windy Street, is our Pub of the Week and has walls lined with photographs and memories of the local area.

It is reportedly haunted by the spirit of a woman known as Lizzie Dees, who is said to have taken her own life on its top floor in the late 1800s.

Today, however, it is a lively community hub, serving food during the week, popular Friday-night pizzas and a rotating selection of cask ales.

The pubs beer garden (Image: The Sun Inn)

We caught up with staff member Archie Murphy.

Introduce yourself

My name is Archie Murphy and I have been up the pub for four years.

Describe the pub

It’s a very old building. All the pictures on the wall are local stuff — it’s from about 100 years back and all that sort of stuff. It’s supposedly haunted as well.

The story is from a girl called Lizzie Dees. In the late 1800s, a woman killed herself on the top floor of the pub in the village.

Do you do food?

A pizza at The Sun Inn (Image: The Sun Inn)

We run food service five days a week, and then every Friday is pizza night. We do eating in and takeaway.

Last week I think we made 95 pizza bases and we sold about 80-something of them in the space of about four hours.

Do you host any events?

Yeah, we get parties in quite a lot. Whenever the village hall has an event up there — karaoke and all that sort of stuff — we get a lot of the drinkers coming down to the pub.

A Sunday Road at the pub (Image: The Sun Inn)

What have you got on draught?

We have Carling, Black Stag Stout, Thatchers Gold, Guinness, Madri, Peroni, Staropramen, and then Czech beer from Prague.

We have Birra Moretti, and then cask ales. We have four pumps for the cask ales and have a rotation every week.

We have a home amber as well — handcrafted home amber — and one of the rotations for the home amber always tends to stay on.

Have you got an outdoor space?

We have quite a big beer garden. It’s all resin floors, and right at the end of the beer garden we have a small outbuilding with leather seats, tables and all that sort of stuff.

Opposite the pub itself, just past the beer garden, we have the pizza bar, which is where we make the pizzas.

We also hold events and stuff in there. If someone’s booked in for a big group, they’ll all go into the pizza bar.

The pizza bar (Image: The Sun Inn)

What is the best thing about working in the pub?

It’s probably the locals. We’re a smaller village, so 90 per cent of the people who come in for drinks and meals, everyone knows each other. It’s like a community, really.
